en: The Philippine eagle, our national bird, has a unique shaggy crest and can only successfully reproduce once every two years.
President Emilio Aguinaldo was exactly 29 years old when he proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite.
The Philippine Senate is the only branch of government that acts as an impeachment court, requiring a two-thirds vote to convict an official.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces over 2,000 years ago by carving the mountains using simple hand tools and moving earth manually.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a makeshift incubator using two native bamboo baskets and hot water bottles to help rural babies survive.
Before the Spanish arrived, many Filipinos wrote on leaves and bamboo using Baybayin, an ancient alphabetic script with 17 distinct characters.
During Bacolod's MassKara Festival, locals wear massive, smiling masks to celebrate their resilience after a tragic ferry sinking and a sugar crisis.
National hero Jose Rizal was a polyglot who could converse in 22 different languages, including Latin, Japanese, and ancient Greek.
The Philippine Bill of Rights specifically forbids the government from imprisoning anyone solely because they cannot pay a debt or a poll tax.
The Philippine flag is the only national flag in the world that is flown with the red stripe on top during a state of war.
The traditional Bayanihan practice literally involved a community physically carrying a family's entire nipa hut on bamboo poles to a new location.
National Artist Fernando Amorsolo famously painted Philippine landscapes using his unique backlighting technique, where the sun shines brightly from behind his subjects.
